\section[die Scheidung]{die Scheidung — the divorce}

\label{lesson:GE-C300-scheidung}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the German for the wedding ceremony, then the German for the registry office.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: die Scheidung}
\textbf{die Scheidung} — \textquotedblleft{}the divorce\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Nach der Scheidung zog er in eine kleine Wohnung.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{After the divorce he moved into a small flat.}
\end{quote}

Plural: \emph{die Scheidungen}. \emph{Geschieden} — divorced — is already known.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{Scheidung} is built on \emph{scheiden} \textquotedblleft{}to separate\textquotedblright{}, from Old High German \emph{sceidan}, Proto-Germanic \emph{skaiþaną} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{die Scheidung}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{die Scheidung}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{die Scheidung}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the German for the wedding ceremony, then the German for the registry office, then say \emph{die Scheidung} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does die Scheidung mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The divorce\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[scheiden]{scheiden — to divorce, as sich scheiden lassen; to part}

\label{lesson:GE-C300-scheiden}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the German for the registry office, then the German for the divorce.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: scheiden}
\textbf{scheiden} — \textquotedblleft{}to divorce, as sich scheiden lassen; to part\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Meine Eltern ließen sich scheiden, als ich zehn war.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{My parents got divorced when I was ten.}
\end{quote}

In this sense with \emph{lassen}: \emph{sich scheiden lassen}. Strong verb: \emph{schied}, \emph{geschieden}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{scheiden} is inherited from Old High German \emph{sceidan}, which EtymDB traces to Proto-Germanic \emph{skaiþaną} \textquotedblleft{}to separate, to divide\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{scheiden}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{scheiden}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{scheiden}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the German for the registry office, then the German for the divorce, then say \emph{scheiden} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does scheiden mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To divorce, as sich scheiden lassen; to part\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[die Trennung]{die Trennung — the separation, the break-up}

\label{lesson:GE-C300-trennung}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the German for the divorce, then the German for to divorce.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: die Trennung}
\textbf{die Trennung} — \textquotedblleft{}the separation, the break-up\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Die Trennung war für beide schwer.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The separation was hard for both.}
\end{quote}

Plural: \emph{die Trennungen}. Built on \emph{trennen}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{Trennung} is built on \emph{trennen} \textquotedblleft{}to separate\textquotedblright{}, from Old High German \emph{trennen}, Proto-Germanic \emph{trannijaną} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[adoptieren]{adoptieren — to adopt}

\label{lesson:GE-C300-adoptieren}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the German for to divorce, then the German for the separation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: adoptieren}
\textbf{adoptieren} — \textquotedblleft{}to adopt\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Sie adoptierten zwei Kinder.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{They adopted two children.}
\end{quote}

Regular, without \emph{ge-}: \emph{hat adoptiert}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{adoptieren} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{adoptāre} \textquotedblleft{}to adopt\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), built on \emph{optāre} \textquotedblleft{}to choose\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{adoptieren}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{adoptieren}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{adoptieren}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the German for to divorce, then the German for the separation, then say \emph{adoptieren} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does adoptieren mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To adopt\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[erleben]{erleben — to go through, to experience}

\label{lesson:GE-C300-erleben}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the German for the separation, then the German for to adopt.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: erleben}
\textbf{erleben} — \textquotedblleft{}to go through, to experience\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
In diesem Jahr erlebte die Familie viel.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{That year the family went through a lot.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Das Erlebnis}, already known, is built on it.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{erleben} is built on \emph{leben} \textquotedblleft{}to live\textquotedblright{}, from Proto-Germanic \emph{libjaną} (EtymDB), with \emph{er-}: to live through.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
